title: Missingness: MCAR, MAR & MNAR
interviewAnswer: Missing values can be completely random, explainable by observed variables, or related to the missing value itself. The mechanism matters because naive imputation can bias estimates and hide useful missingness signals.
keyPoints: MAR: missingness depends on observed variables.
MNAR: missingness depends on unobserved/missing value.
why: Missingness: MCAR, MAR & MNAR appears frequently in data-science work because it connects mathematical assumptions to practical decisions, diagnostics and failure modes.
deepDive: Missing values can be completely random, explainable by observed variables, or related to the missing value itself. The mechanism matters because naive imputation can bias estimates and hide useful missingness signals. MAR: missingness depends on observed variables. MNAR: missingness depends on unobserved/missing value. A strong practitioner separates the modeling assumption from the estimation procedure, checks diagnostics rather than trusting a single score, and explains what would make the method inappropriate.
workedExample: Income nonresponse may be related to income itself, making simple mean imputation particularly questionable.
commonMistakes: Applying the method without checking its assumptions or data-generating process.
Choosing it because it is familiar rather than comparing against an appropriate baseline.
